Module  java.base

Class Scanner

  • java.lang.Object
    • java.util.Scanner
  • All implemented interfaces
    Closeable ， AutoCloseable ， Iterator<String> 
    public final class Scanner
extends Object
implements Iterator<String>, Closeable
    A simple text scanner that can parse primitive types and strings using regular expressions.

    ScannerIts input is broken into tokens using a delimiter pattern, which by default matches whitespace. The obtained token can then be converted into values of various different types.nextmethod.

    For example, this code allows the user toSystem.inReads number: 

    
     Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
     int i = sc.nextInt();

    As another example, this code allows from a filemyNumbersentry allocationlongType: 

    
      Scanner sc = new Scanner(new File("myNumbers"));
      while (sc.hasNextLong()) {
          long aLong = sc.nextLong();
      }

    The scanner can also use delimiters other than whitespace. This example reads several items from a string: 

    
     String input = "1 fish 2 fish red fish blue fish";
     Scanner s = new Scanner(input).useDelimiter("\\s*fish\\s*");
     System.out.println(s.nextInt());
     System.out.println(s.nextInt());
     System.out.println(s.next());
     System.out.println(s.next());
     s.close();

    prints the following output: 

    
     1
     2
     red
     blue

    The same output can be produced using this code, which parses all four tokens at once using a regular expression: 

    
     String input = "1 fish 2 fish red fish blue fish";
     Scanner s = new Scanner(input);
     s.findInLine("(\\d+) fish (\\d+) fish (\\w+) fish (\\w+)");
     MatchResult result = s.match();
     for (int i=1; i<=result.groupCount(); i++)
         System.out.println(result.group(i));
     s.close();

    4502201395911Identifies what the scanner usesdefault whitespace delimiter 。 reset()The method resets the value of the scanner delimiter to the default whitespace delimiter, regardless of whether it has been previously changed.

    The scan operation may block while waiting for input.

    next()andhasNext()method and its companion methods (e.g.nextInt()andhasNextInt()) It first skips any input matching the delimiter pattern, and then attempts to return the next token. hasNext()andnext()methods may block waiting for further input. hasNext()whether the method block is associated with itsnext()whether the method will blocknext() 。 tokens()The method may also block waiting for input.

    offindInLine() ， findWithinHorizon() ， skip(), andfindAll()The independent operation of the method's delimiter pattern. These methods will attempt to match the specified pattern regardless of separators in the input, so they can be used in special cases where separators are irrelevant. These methods may block waiting for more input.

    when the scanner throwsInputMismatchExceptionwhenthe scanner will not pass the token that caused the exception, so it can be retrieved or skipped by other methods.

    Depending on the type of delimiter pattern, empty tokens can be returned. For example, the pattern"\\s+"An empty token will not be returned, because it matches multiple instances of the delimiter. "\\s"Mode"\\s"An empty token can be returned because it only passes through one space at a time.

    Localized numbers

    Instances of this class can scan numbers in the standard format as well as in the format of the scanner's locale. scannerinitial localeYesLocale.getDefault(Locale.Category.FORMAT)the value returned by the method; It can be changed viauseLocale()method changes. reset()The method resets the value of the scanner's locale to the initial locale, regardless of whether it was previously changed.

    The localized format is defined according to the following parameters, which for a particular locale are taken from that locale's.DecimalFormatObjectdfAnd itsDecimalFormatSymbolsObjectdfs 。

    LocalGroupSeparator  
    The character used to separate thousands groups, i.e.,  dfs. getGroupingSeparator()
    LocalDecimalSeparator  
    The character used for the decimal point, i.e.,  dfs. getDecimalSeparator()
    LocalPositivePrefix  
    The string that appears before a positive number (may be empty), i.e.,  df. getPositivePrefix()
    LocalPositiveSuffix  
    The string that appears after a positive number (may be empty), i.e.,  df. getPositiveSuffix()
    LocalNegativePrefix  
    The string that appears before a negative number (may be empty), i.e.,  df. getNegativePrefix()
    LocalNegativeSuffix  
    The string that appears after a negative number (may be empty), i.e.,  df. getNegativeSuffix()
    LocalNaN  
    The string that represents not-a-number for floating-point values, i.e.,  dfs. getNaN()
    LocalInfinity  
    The string that represents infinity for floating-point values, i.e.,  dfs. getInfinity()

      • nextLine

        public String nextLine()
        Advances this scanner past the current line and returns the skipped input. This method returns the rest of the current line, excluding any line separator at the end. The position is set to the beginning of the next line.

        Since this method continues to search the input to find line separators, if no line separator exists, it can buffer all input in order to search for the line to skip.

        Result
        skipped rows
        Exception
        NoSuchElementException- If no line is found
        IllegalStateException- If this scanner is closed

      • findWithinHorizon

        public String findWithinHorizon​(Pattern pattern,
                                int horizon)
        Attempts to find the next match of the specified pattern.

        This method searches the input up to the specified search range, ignoring delimiters. If a pattern is found, the scanner advances past the matched input and returns the string that matches the pattern. If no such pattern is detected, it returns null and the scanner's position remains unchanged. This method may block waiting for input that matches the pattern.

        The scanner will never search beyond its current positionhorizoncode point. Note that the match may be limited by the horizon; In other words, if the horizon is large, any matching result may differ. The scanner treats the horizon as a transparent non-anchored boundary (seeMatcher.useTransparentBounds(boolean)andMatcher.useAnchoringBounds(boolean) ）。

        If horizon is0, then the horizon is ignored, and this method continues to search the input for the specified pattern without bound. In this case, it may buffer all input searched for the pattern.

        If the horizon is negative, throws IllegalArgumentException.

        Parameter
        pattern- The pattern to scan
        horizon- Search range
        Result
        The text that matches the specified pattern
        Exception
        IllegalStateException- If this scanner is closed
        IllegalArgumentException- If the horizon is negative

      • skip

        public Scanner skip​(Pattern pattern)
        Skips input that matches the specified pattern, ignoring delimiters. If the anchored match of the specified pattern succeeds, this method will skip the input.

        If no match for the specified pattern is found at the current position, no input is skipped and an exception is thrown.NoSuchElementException 。

        Since this method attempts to match the specified pattern starting from the scanner's current position, patterns that can match a large amount of input (such as ".*") may cause the scanner to buffer a large amount of input.

        Note that by using a pattern that cannot match (for example,sc.skip("[ \t]*")skip some content without riskingNoSuchElementExceptionthe risk.

        Parameter
        pattern- The string specifying the pattern to skip
        Result
        this scanner
        Exception
        NoSuchElementException- If the specified pattern is not found
        IllegalStateException- If this scanner is closed

      • tokens

        public Stream<String> tokens()
        Returns a stream of delimiter-separated tokens from this scanner. This stream contains the same tokens that would be returned starting from the current state of this scanner, by repeatedly callingnext()method, untilhasNext()The method returns false.

        The resulting stream is sequential and ordered. All stream elements are non-null.

        Begins scanning using the current state of this scanner when a terminal stream operation is initiated. Pairclose()andioException()Subsequent calls to any method on this scanner other than this one may return undefined results, or may have an indeterminate effect on the returned stream. Returns the source of the streamSpliteratorYesfail-fast ， AlsoIf any such call is detected during execution of the stream pipeline, it will make a best effort to throwConcurrentModificationException 。

        After the stream pipeline execution completes, this scanner will be in an indeterminate state and cannot be reused.

        If this scanner contains resources that must be released, it should be released by calling itsclose()method or by closing the returned stream to close this scanner. Closing the stream will close the underlying scanner. If this scanner is closed when this method is invoked, or if this scanner is closed during stream pipeline execution, then this method throws.IllegalStateException 。

        This method may block waiting for more input.

        API Note:
        For example, the following code creates a comma-separated list of tokens from a string: 
           List<String> result = new Scanner("abc,def,,ghi") .useDelimiter(",") .tokens() .collect(Collectors.toList());

        the result list will contain"abc" ， "def", empty string, and"ghi" 。

        Result
        The continuous stream of token strings
        Exception
        IllegalStateException- If this scanner is closed
        Starting from the following version:
        9
